prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1444; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a report that the insured's vehicle was sideswiped while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The claimant's attorney has notified our office that they will handle all further contact on the bodily injury portion.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver is listed as a named driver and that coverage was in force at the time of loss. No issues with the policy status were found.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the lane change collision as described by the other driver.

Entry 4: Spoke with two independent witnesses who each saw the sideswipe occur and gave accounts consistent with the other driver's statement.

Entry 5: Reviewed scene photographs and the damage estimate. The damage pattern along the passenger side matches the impact described by all parties, and no prior damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 6: Claimant reported neck and upper back pain with stiffness, consistent with a whiplash-type injury for a collision of this kind. The attorney provided the initial medical records.

Entry 7: Took a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account of how the collision happened matched the account given in every earlier conversation, with no changes in the sequence of events.

Entry 8: Medical file shows the claimant was treated for complaints in the same body area within the past two years. The attorney's office has been asked for those records to clarify how the prior condition interacts with the current complaints.

Entry 9: Received the prior treatment records. The earlier condition is documented, and the physician notes that it may add to the current symptoms, so the current complaints are being evaluated with that in mind.

Entry 10: Treatment followed a typical course of care and tapered as the claimant improved, with reduced visits and decreasing reports of pain over the following weeks.

Entry 11: Reviewed the full file. The reported injury is plausible for a crash of this type, the liability facts are supported by independent sources, and the claim is proceeding to evaluation with the attorney on record.
